title: Scalar projection formula and the Tor bound for an open immersion
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $A$ a
finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open
immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $d\ge\operatorname{cd}(j)$
([def-kun-cd]; finite by [lem-kun-0f10]). Let
$K\in D(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in the sense of
[def-kun-tor-amplitude]: $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AN)=0$ for
$r\notin[a,b]$ and every $A$-module sheaf $N$ on $U_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then:

1. for every $A$-module $M$, with constant sheaves $\underline M_X$,
   $\underline M_U=j^*\underline M_X$, the projection morphism

   $$
   (Rj_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A\underline M_X\longrightarrow
   Rj_*\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A\underline M_U\bigr)
   $$

   is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$;
2. $Rj_*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$;
3. $Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_U^*K\cong\nu_X^*Rj_*K$ has Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+d]$ against every module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

Here schemes over $k$ are as in [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and finite type is as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], open immersions as in [def-weil-open-immersion], and separable closedness as in [def-kun-separably-closed]. Use the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the constant sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf], ordinary uncompleted derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the projection morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The morphisms $\nu_U,\nu_X$ are the comparison morphisms [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; pro-étale Tor amplitude means the all-module-sheaf test [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The interval endpoints $a,b$ are integers and $d$ is a nonnegative integer. For an empty interval, on either site the Tor-amplitude assertion means the same displayed vanishing test in every degree; in particular the zero object satisfies it. This extends the nonempty-interval convention of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] without imposing an extra inequality on $a,b$.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes U and X locally Noetherian. Quasi-compactness of aU makes U compact; the standard locally-Noetherian and quasi-compact-source instances give QuasiCompact j and QuasiSeparated j. The l-primary hypothesis gives IsAddTorsion A because l^n is positive. Apply the finite-cohomological-dimension theorem to the morphism over the separably closed field.

source.place: Main proof: geometry and torsion coefficient hypotheses

proof.text: Prove the actual canonical projection morphism, not merely existence of an object isomorphism. Fix K and whisker the projection natural transformation in its second variable with the exact derived constant-sheaf functor C:D(A) to D(X_et,A). The two resulting triangulated functors preserve all coproducts: Rj_* does by finite cohomological dimension, while derived pullback, tensor, and constants do by their adjunctions. The projection transformation commutes with shifts. At A[0], use the canonical monoidal identification C(A[0]) with the tensor unit and the projection-unit theorem. The ring generates D(A) under coproducts, triangles, shifts and retracts. Thus the transformation is invertible everywhere. In Lean the source-library isIso_of_isIso_app_singleFunctor_obj_self is the direct natural-transformation criterion for this existing generation statement. Apply it at M[0] and transport through the exact-functor single-object comparison to obtain clause (1) for every M.

Extract the numerical bound on classical module-sheaf higher direct image. The set of natural torsion-abelian bounds defining cd(j) has nonempty finite part since its infimum is at most d. The well-ordering of extended natural numbers makes that infimum a member, giving a bound n at most d. The underlying abelian sheaf of any A-module sheaf is torsion since A is finite. The module-abelian comparison, together with the single-sheaf/classical-derived-functor comparison and exactness of forgetting through homology, identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of R^q j_*S with the vanishing bounded-below abelian direct-image homology for q>d. Faithfulness of forgetting reflects zero objects. This yields the hypothesis of the derived-functor upper-amplitude lemma.

Convert the given explicit all-sheaf Tor predicate to the source categorical predicate. By the finite-ring Jacobson test, it suffices to test Rj_*K against the constant module kappa=A/Jac(A). Clause (1), already established for every M, identifies this tensor with Rj_*(K tensor kappa_U). The input all-sheaf test puts K tensor kappa_U in degrees [a,b]. Left t-exactness of the right derived functor gives the lower bound a. The classical bound in the preceding step and the derived-functor upper-amplitude lemma give the upper bound b+d. The residue criterion gives the all-module-sheaf bound on Rj_*K. These arguments apply unchanged to a>b; no separate nonempty-interval assumption occurs.

The all-sheaf Tor hypothesis gives K in D^{>=a}, by testing the tensor unit. Apply the bounded-below etale/pro-etale direct-image comparison to obtain the isomorphism e:Rj_proet,* nu_U^* K ≅ nu_X^* Rj_et,*K. Use the forward comparison Tor-amplitude theorem on the just-proved etale bound, and transport along e to give the pro-etale all-sheaf bound. The source forward comparison interface is formulated for every pair of integer endpoints and the actual module categories, so it also covers empty intervals and avoids the ULift/intrinsic-presentation wrapper. Return the four clauses as a conjunction.

I checked them against the main-20261015 item and its proof, the unit _section/proof, and Stacks 0F12 (etale-cohomology.tex l.20164), 0F10 (l.20041) and 09A6 (proetale.tex l.4696). No SGA is cited. The statement change only replaces the reference def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude with def-kun-tor-amplitude. The old reference is about local O_E/ϖ^n coefficients and constructible pro-étale objects, so it does not fit an étale K with an arbitrary finite ℓ-primary A such as F_ℓ×F_ℓ. The displayed all-sheaf test, every hypothesis and all three clauses are unchanged, so nothing is weakened. The empty-interval sentence is a convention only, and step 1 handles that case (K=0). On the pro-étale side the coefficient category and Tor notion are the same pair lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval already uses. Steps: (2) the Noetherian/qcqs facts, quasi-compactness of the basis V→X (no affine intersections assumed) and 0F10(1),(2) are correct. (3) the hypotheses of thm-sp-truncation-e2 are met; the module-to-abelian bridge feeds def-kun-cd; the support gives [a,b+d]. (4) restriction and j_* both preserve K-injectives; (j_*I)|_V = j_{V,*}(I|_{V_U}) sectionwise. (5) the mate compatibility with the definitional maps is written out; it is elementary, and lem-kun-0f12 cites def-kun-constant-projection-morphism, so its canonical map is P_V. (6) 0F12 holds for unbounded objects and any M. (7) the detection is unbounded and goes through exact sheafification on a basis. (8)-(9) constant tests, stalks as pullbacks, conservativity on the étale site only. (10) K∈D^+, Q bounded and j qcqs before the comparison theorem; the interval [a,b+d] is nonempty. Edge cases checked: empty j, j=id with d=0, K=0, a>b, negative endpoints, F_ℓ×F_ℓ, infinite-rank M, Z/ℓ² with M=Z/ℓ. There are no new nodes; the rg search found no duplicate of clause (1) or (2), and there is no cycle. All declared tool_uses are generic interfaces and are accepted; 0F10 and 0F12 are on this unit's route in main-20261015. The stale unit record (still the master version, chapter sec-six-functors) is correctly left for the maintainer. No fixes.

reviewed_lean.note: Every hypothesis and conclusion of the node matches the Lean: separably closed k, l prime with l ≠ ringChar k, finite l-primary A : Type (u+1), finite-type structure maps with j ≫ aX = aU and IsOpenImmersion j, cd(j) ≤ d using the same qc/qs witness terms as lem-kun-0f10, K with the recorded etale hasTorAmplitudeIn in [a,b]. Clause 1 is IsIso of rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap at the degree-0 constant sheaf. Clause 2 is etale Tor amplitude [a,b+d] of rightDerivedLowerStar. Clause 3 is Nonempty(Rj_proet* nu_U^*K ≅ nu_X^* Rj_*K) together with pro-etale torAmplitudeIn [a,b+d] against all sheaves. No extra hypotheses, universes bound. Edge cases checked: a>b (all-degree vanishing, matching the node's convention), a=b, negative endpoints, d=0 with j=id, empty U, zero ring, char 0, M=0 and M of infinite rank. Non-blocking observations: (1) clause 3 uses the existing ProEtale.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (record def-sf-categorical-proetale-tor-amplitude) rather than the recorded HasCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude, which builds in a<=b and cannot express the node's empty-interval convention; it is an existing declaration, not a private copy, and the fixed-ring encoding and comparisonUpperStar match the recorded proetale-modules and site-comparison records; (2) explicit structure maps are used instead of Scheme.Over/IsOver, with the same content.
